primary_prior_art.work: A Distribution Testing Approach to Clustering Distributions
primary_prior_art.scope: global finite-sample recovery of a hidden partition of multiple discrete distributions under exact within-cluster equality and total-variation separation

public_code.classification: peer-reviewed theory and public paper confirmed; no immutable paper-specific author implementation confirmed; not an executable action-conditioned full-consequence B4 estimator

findings: global transitive recovery of clusters of sampled distributions is existing prior art under exact within-cluster equality and between-cluster TV separation
the result covers both unknown cluster distributions and extends to a constant number of clusters
pairwise-testing inconsistency is not a universal barrier to global partition recovery
the fixed observed-alphabet distribution-clustering problem does not implement recursive greatest-bisimulation refinement over unknown successor blocks
independent per-action global clusterings need not define one common controlled partition
exact within-cluster equality does not define the tolerance-indexed approximate ontology required by LBQ001-B4
the result does not provide action coverage, semantic-channel independence, Q recovery, or denotation d
counterexamples: states with disjoint raw-successor identities can be bisimilar after successor states are quotiented, so clustering raw transition distributions can over-separate even with infinite data
three distributions near a tolerance boundary show that exact latent-class clustering does not select a block-diameter, representative-radius, or connected-component approximate ontology
two actions can induce incompatible global partitions whose common action-complete refinement is singleton, so per-action clustering is insufficient
decision_text: Global transitive partition recovery from samples is existing prior art when distributions are exactly identical within clusters and separated in total variation, but this does not supply action-complete coverage, recursive greatest controlled quotient recovery, approximate within-block semantics, or language-target coupling.
